    ProblemDetail:

        type:

          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'

        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp

          format: date-time

## Summary

When an owner is created, the application now counts how many existing owners share the same last name at that moment and returns it as the integer field `namesakeCount` in the owner response.

Following the established pattern for the other creation-time computed fields (`membershipNumber`, `customerCode`, `membershipTier`), I made these changes:

- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — computes the count via a new `countNamesakes(lastName)` helper (streams existing owners, matching last name exactly, excluding the not-yet-persisted new owner) and sets it on the owner before saving.
- **`model/Owner.java`** — added a persisted `namesakeCount` field (`@Column(name = "namesake_count")`) with getter/setter.
- **`openapi.yml`** — added the `namesakeCount` property to the `Owner` schema (readOnly int32, min 0), so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct auto-maps it by name.
- **DB schemas** (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres) — added the `namesake_count` column.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1Tests`** — added two tests: `0` for a unique last name, and `1`/`2` as owners accumulate under the same last name.

Verified: `290 tests run, 0 failures, BUILD SUCCESS`.
